incidente.resumo: On June 12, 2025, Google Cloud, Google Workspace and Google Security Operations returned increased 503 errors on external API requests globally. A policy change with blank fields, replicated globally, hit a new Service Control code path without error handling or feature flag protection, causing a crash loop. A red-button disabled the path within 40 minutes; us-central-1 took up to about 2h40 to recover because restarting tasks overloaded the underlying Spanner table.

descricao.texto: The SRE team was triaging the incident within 2 minutes.
trechos: Within 2 minutes, our Site Reliability Engineering team was triaging the incident.

gatilho.texto: A policy change with unintended blank fields was inserted into the regional Spanner tables used by Service Control and replicated globally within seconds.
trechos: a policy change was inserted into the regional Spanner tables that Service Control uses for policies.
This policy data contained unintended blank fields.

descricao.texto: A new Service Control quota policy code path had no appropriate error handling and no feature flag; the blank fields caused a null pointer that crashed the binaries in every region.
trechos: The issue with this change was that it did not have appropriate error handling nor was it feature flag protected.
Without the appropriate error handling, the null pointer caused the binary to crash.
This occurred globally given each regional deployment.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The failing code path was never exercised during the region-by-region rollout because it needed a policy change to trigger it.
trechos: the code path that failed was never exercised during this rollout due to needing a policy change that would trigger the code.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Policy metadata is replicated globally within seconds.
trechos: Given the global nature of quota management, this metadata was replicated globally within seconds.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Service Control lacked randomized exponential backoff, so restarting tasks created a herd effect that overloaded the Spanner table in large regions.
trechos: as Service Control tasks restarted, it created a herd effect on the underlying infrastructure it depends on (i.e. that Spanner table), overloading the infrastructure.
Service Control did not have the appropriate randomized exponential backoff implemented to avoid this.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The Cloud Service Health infrastructure was down, delaying the first incident report by about an hour.
trechos: due to the Cloud Service Health infrastructure being down due to this outage.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: Some customers' monitoring running on Google Cloud also failed, leaving them without a signal.
trechos: For some customers, the monitoring infrastructure they had running on Google Cloud was also failing

descricao.texto: A new Service Control feature for additional quota policy checks, released on May 29, 2025, triggered by the June 12 policy change with blank fields.
trechos: On May 29, 2025, a new feature was added to Service Control for additional quota policy checks.
This policy data contained unintended blank fields.

passos.texto: Root cause identified within 10 minutes and the red-button to disable the serving path prepared.
trechos: Within 10 minutes, the root cause was identified and the red-button (to disable the serving path) was being put in place.

passos.texto: Red-button rollout completed within 40 minutes; smaller regions recovered first.
trechos: Within 40 minutes of the incident, the red-button rollout was completed, and we started seeing recovery across regions, starting with the smaller ones first.

passos.texto: In us-central-1, task creation was throttled and traffic routed to multi-regional databases to reduce load.
trechos: as we throttled task creation to minimize the impact on the underlying infrastructure and routed traffic to multi-regional databases to reduce the load.

acoes.texto: Freeze changes to the Service Control stack and manual policy pushes until remediation is complete.
trechos: Immediately upon recovery, we froze all changes to the Service Control stack and manual policy pushes until we can completely remediate the system.

acoes.texto: Modularize Service Control so checks are isolated and fail open.
trechos: We will modularize Service Control’s architecture, so the functionality is isolated and fails open.

acoes.texto: Propagate globally replicated data incrementally with time to validate and detect issues.
trechos: data replication needs to be propagated incrementally with sufficient time to validate and detect issues.

acoes.texto: Require feature flags, disabled by default, for all changes to critical binaries.
trechos: We will enforce all changes to critical binaries to be feature flag protected and disabled by default.

acoes.texto: Improve static analysis and testing for error handling.
trechos: We will improve our static analysis and testing practices to correctly handle errors and if need be fail open.

acoes.texto: Ensure systems use randomized exponential backoff.
trechos: We will audit and ensure our systems employ randomized exponential backoff.

acoes.texto: Keep monitoring and communication infrastructure working even when Google Cloud is down.
trechos: We'll ensure our monitoring and communication infrastructure remains operational to serve customers even when Google Cloud and our primary monitoring products are down, ensuring business continuity.
**Duration:** 3 hours

motivo_confianca_baixa: categoria_causa: software-bug (missing error handling) vs configuration-error (policy change with blank fields). Also note the preliminary mini report described the cause differently ('invalid automated quota update') than the final report.
